name: _pcWatch
detail: uint[] { 0x1B00, // OPCOM subfunction handler (ND->68K) 0x250E, // nd_host_interrupt_handler (scans ND channel flags 0x0B56 on a kick) 0x5C42, // RCVCOMPLETE (LANCE RX complete) 0xBED8, // XMRECEIVER 0xBFF8, // shared message-delivery primitive (the ONLY path to the superkick producer) 0xC2CC, // jsr 0xEAA6 site 0xEAA6, // superkick producer entry 0xEACC, // superkick ring write + SCIP 0xEF0180 // ---- RX-FORWARD DECISION (RCVCOMPLETE 0x5C42 tail @0x601A) ---- // Byte-verified: after RCVCOMPLETE processes the descriptor it reaches the branch at // 0x601A `tst.l $18(a6); beq 0x6034`. $18(a6) is the message buffer RCVCOMPLETE built. // * $18(a6) != 0 -> 0x6020: jsr 0x134E6 = ENQUEUE message to the ND-100 ready-ring // ($188D6) and signal (this is the ONLY path that leads to a SCIP/ // superkick to the ND-100) => the frame reaches XMSG. = DELIVERED. // * $18(a6) == 0 -> 0x6034: bsr 0x5B60 (RCVRINGAPP, re-append the RX buffer) + `jmp // (a5)` yield, with NO 0x134E6 call, NO SCIP. = DISCARDED. // $18(a6) is cleared (frame discarded) by ANY of the three gates in RCVCOMPLETE: // 0x5DF6 `beq 0x5EF4` gate1: dst-MAC recheck vs card MAC ($1885E) ($38(a6)==0) // 0x5DFE `beq 0x5EF4` gate2: frame is NOT IEEE-802.3 length-framed ($36(a6)==0) // (COSMOS is 802.3: bytes 12-13 = payload LENGTH, not a DIX // EtherType; a 0x0800/0x0806 typed frame is dropped here) // 0x5E0A `beq 0x5EF4` / 0x5E18 `beq 0x5ECA` gate3: NO free XMSG receive buffer in // the pool at $188C6 (+0 count word / +4 free-list head). // Watching both branch targets pins EXACTLY which happens for a given inbound frame. 0x6020, // RX DELIVERED (jsr 0x134E6 -> ND-100 ready-ring + SCIP) 0x6034, // RX DISCARDED (re-append RX buffer, yield, NO SCIP to ND-100) // ---- RX NO-BUFFER DISCARD (firmware RE 2026-07-24, ENNS0-RXPOOL-PRODUCER doc) ---- // Ground truth from the 68K firmware: the rx pool at $188C6 is NOT pre-filled by // firmware init (rxpool_init @0x5512 zeroes it). It is ENABLED by a host command // (count:=1 @0x67DA) and FILLED only by the host POST-BUFFER command (opcode 0x12 // @0x6CEE -> PLANC_APPD 0x134E6 pushes onto freehead $188CA). So gate3's count!=0 // test can PASS (enabled) while freehead is STILL NULL (host posted no buffer). In // that case RCVCOMPLETE branches 0x5E18 -> 0x5ECA: bump the miss counter and DISCARD // with NO SCIP. This is a DIFFERENT drop than the generic 0x6034, and it is the exact // "enabled-but-starved" failure mode to look for on a node that receives but never // forwards. Watching 0x5ECA distinguishes "host never posted a receive buffer" from // "wrong MAC / not 802.3". 0x5ECA, // RX NO-BUFFER DISCARD (pool enabled, freehead null) - host posted no rx buffer // ---- RX-POOL HOST-COMMAND HANDLERS (COSMOS-ETHERNET-LINK-CONTROL-FRAMES-2026-08-03 §2g) ---- // The pool is HOST-fed: 0x67DA is the ENABLE command handler (idempotent - re-enable with // the same parameter is OK, a different one returns -17 and changes nothing), and 0x6CEE is // the POST-BUFFER handler for host command opcode 0x12 - the ONLY code that ever pushes a // node back onto rxpool_freehead ($188CA, at 0x6CFE inside it). Watching these answers the // open question from ND_EthernetII_LINK_FRAMES_AND_RXPOOL_HANDOFF_2026-08-04 §5.2: does the // 0x12 command reach the firmware at all, and does SINTRAN keep posting or stop? If 0x5ECA // fires while 0x6CEE has gone quiet, the host stopped replenishing; if 0x6CEE NEVER fires, // the command is being lost on the way in (our transport bug). 0x67DA, // RX-POOL ENABLE handler (host command; sets $188C6 count:=1 + parameter word) 0x6CEE, // POST-BUFFER handler (host opcode 0x12; pushes a node onto freehead $188CA) // ---- RX GATE PROGRESS (firmware dis 0x5D60..0x5E1C, verified 2026-07-24) ---- // The three RCVCOMPLETE gates are sequential fall-throughs: // 0x5DF6 beq 0x5EF4 gate1: frame dst MAC (frame+0x30) must equal the firmware // station MAC at 0x1885E (unicast) OR promiscuous 0x18888!=0. // 0x5DFA (reached only if gate1 PASSED) tst $36 -> gate2 (802.3 length-framed). // 0x5E02 (reached only if gate2 PASSED) -> gate3 (pool count / freehead). // 0x5EF4 common gate-FAIL convergence (gate1/gate2/gate3-count all land here). // Watching the fall-through PCs pins EXACTLY how far a frame got before it died. 0x5DFA, // gate1 PASSED (dst MAC matched 0x1885E) -> now testing gate2 0x5E02, // gate2 PASSED (802.3) -> now testing gate3 (pool) 0x5EF4, // a gate FAILED -> discard (which one = one past the last "PASSED" line) // ---- RESET_ENTRY / PRKEY-PUBLISH window (PRKEY_INVESTIGATION_PROMPT_2026-07-27 §4.2) ---- // The RE agent's execution breakpoints for the cold-start publication path. Watching // these pins EXACTLY which branch reset_entry takes and whether the publisher completes, // so the "did the firmware publish PRKEY?" question is answered from the PC trace alone. // reset_entry(0x1CFE): cmpi.l #0x55555555,(0x04BA) / bne cold. Warm branch -> 0x1D58 area. 0x1CFE, // reset_entry taken (68K left reset) 0x1D26, // about to test the warm-restart signature (0x04BA) 0x1D58, // COLD-branch target: bne TAKEN (0x04BA != 0x55555555) -> cold start (leads to publisher) 0x1D9C, // COLD path started (leads to the publisher) 0x1DA0, // jsr 0x1AD4 returned 0x1DA6, // about to jsr 0x1C6A (the datafield-table + PRKEY publisher) 0x1C6A, // publisher ENTERED 0x1CF4, // publisher reached the PRKEY store (move.w #0x5473,(0x0404)) 0x1DAA, // PRKEY written OK -> clr warm sig (cold start succeeded) 0x1DB0, // STARTED := 1 (0x04C0) 0x1DBC, // monitor reply := 3 (0x040C) cold-start-done }
